questions: Do you have a history of Parkinson's disease?
Are you currently taking any medications for tremors or movement disorders?
Do you feel that your hands shake more when they are resting in your lap compared to when you reach for an object?
Have you noticed any stiffness in your muscles or slowness in your movements recently?
orders: Observe the patient's hands at rest in his lap for rhythmic oscillations
Perform finger-to-nose testing to assess for intention tremor and dysmetria
Assess muscle tone for rigidity (cogwheel or lead-pipe) during passive range of motion
Evaluate for bradykinesia using rapid repetitive movements (finger tapping, hand opening/closing)
Check postural reflexes via the pull test
served: surface EMG tremor analysis with accelerometry (frequency, coherence)
results: 1. Observe the patient's hands at rest in his lap for rhythmic oscillations
surface EMG tremor analysis with accelerometry (frequency, coherence): variable frequency, poor coherence between segments
2. Perform finger-to-nose testing to assess for intention tremor and dysmetria
3. Assess muscle tone for rigidity (cogwheel or lead-pipe) during passive range of motion
muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): normal; no cervical dystonic posturing and no sensory trick
4. Evaluate for bradykinesia using rapid repetitive movements (finger tapping, hand opening/closing)
finger-tapping for bradykinesia and decrement: no decrement
5. Check postural reflexes via the pull test
